definitions.ratio: encoded bytes divided by canonical pixel bytes; below 1.0 means smaller
definitions.file_bytes: the size a whole file would occupy: the candidate's payload for every tile it can represent, the raw codec's bytes for every tile it cannot, plus the container framing (a 64-byte header, a 40-byte directory entry plus a 4-byte CRC trailer per tile). Baselines are whole files, so the comparison uses this column.
definitions.raw_fallback_bytes: the canonical bytes of the tiles the candidate cannot represent. A candidate with a non-zero fallback cannot produce a file on its own.
definitions.covers_all_tiles: whether the candidate could represent every tile of the image. When it is false, the candidate's ratio is a partial-file figure and the raw fallback is part of it.
definitions.payload_bytes: the sum of the tile payloads alone, without container framing
definitions.bpp: encoded bytes times eight, divided by canonical pixel bytes
definitions.resolution_class: the smallest ladder entry (512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384) that is at least the image's longest edge
definitions.memory_note: peak_*_alloc_bytes are heap bytes tracked by the harness's own global allocator; they are not process resident set size and exclude the operating system's own overhead
definitions.experimental_note: the experimental codecs are research-only. They are not reachable from get_codec, are not in IMPLEMENTED_CODEC_IDS, and can never appear in a decodable file
definitions.per_tile_note: the per_tile section carries the size and exactness of every tile. The full per-tile record, with the per-tile timings and heap peaks, is kept verbatim under benchmarks/results/research-raw/
definitions.aggregate_note: the aggregate section sums each codec over the images that codec was measured on. A baseline that could not be measured (an image above the pixel cap) is left out of that baseline's aggregate, so the two denominators can differ. The matched_aggregate, matched_per_category and matched_per_resolution sections cover only the images where every codec and every baseline was measured, and they are the comparison to read.

matched_subset.note: the images on which every codec and every baseline was measured; the matched_aggregate, matched_per_category and matched_per_resolution sections cover exactly these images
